item.text: {"winner":"A","confidence":"medium","summary":"A is the less risky patch, mainly because it preserves the existing FilesOption APIs and actually tests retrying Upload from a non-seekable streamed reader. Neither patch satisfies the frozen contract closely enough to merge unchanged.","reasons":["A’s retry test uses io.MultiReader, directly proving Upload buffers streamed content into a replayable multipart body; B tests Upload with an *os.File, so its unrelated seekable-body retry change could make that test pass without buffering.","A leaves the existing WithFilesQuery and WithFilesRequestOptions signatures untouched, whereas B changes their exported return types and introduces FilesRequestOption.","A’s extra upload API is somewhat narrower than B’s arbitrary WithFileFormValue extension, although both improperly add association options.","Both correctly validate basic arguments and verify multipart field name, filename, content, and retry payload consistency."],"risks_a":["Upload has the wrong signature: it accepts ...UploadFileOption instead of the required ...FilesOption.","Upload bypasses FilesService.Add and duplicates request, decoding, and missing-data logic.","It adds prohibited association options and extends multipartbody instead of simply reusing multipartbody.NewFile as required by the contract intent; it also adds an unrelated project association option explicitly outside scope discipline constraints around association fields and unrelated work scope apply here generally, not just project-specific wording? Better phrase directly: adds association machinery forbidden by contract, including project association. Avoid malformed sentence. Need valid final—can't edit? I can formulate full JSON before final. Let's rewrite cleanly."] ,"risks_b":["Upload also has the wrong option type and bypasses FilesService.Add.","It changes existing exported option return types and adds a substantial new option-interface hierarchy.","Its Upload retry test does not establish replayability for non-seekable streamed content, and it lacks a source-reader failure test."]}
